# Training-data poisoning controls for adaptive market forecasters — concept pack (small)

## How it works

- [statement] NIST explains that label-flipping targeted poisoning can insert samples with attacker-chosen labels when the attacker controls the labeling function. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-16) — https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-2e2025.pdf

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Zhang, Zhu and Lessard study online poisoning in which an attacker observes the stream and can contaminate the current training point. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-16) — https://proceedings.mlr.press/v120/zhang20b.html
- [statement] Wang and colleagues distinguish semi-online attacks targeting a final classifier from fully-online attacks targeting loss throughout the stream. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-16) — https://arxiv.org/html/1905.12121v3
- [statement] For the studied online gradient-descent setting, Wang and colleagues find the L2-norm filtering defense permits rapid poisoning. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-16) — https://arxiv.org/html/1905.12121v3
- [statement] The online-defense paper finds that overly restrictive filtering removes clean examples and slows learning, while permissive filtering allows faster poisoning. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-16) — https://arxiv.org/html/1905.12121v3
- [statement] The online-defense study uses BreastCancer, IMDB, MNIST and FashionMNIST datasets in its reported defense comparison. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-16) — https://arxiv.org/html/1905.12121v3
- [statement] NIST lists access controls, data sanitization and validation, and dataset provenance and integrity attestation as ways to mitigate some targeted-poisoning risks. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-16) — https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-2e2025.pdf
- [statement] NIST describes robust-training mitigations including model ensembles with voting and robust optimization with trimmed loss. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-16) — https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/ai/NIST.AI.100-2e2025.pdf
- [statement] The influence-defense study reports that changing clean high-influence data points can reduce accuracy; defensive transformations can lose useful information. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-16) — https://arxiv.org/html/2104.13230
